newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh prison riots continue, spread.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh prison riots continue, spread.

text.p: A Bangladesh jail revolt entered its fourth day on Thursday with nearly 2,000 armed police and paramilitary troops on alert around the complex, police said.
Prisoners, angered by being left out of an independence day amnesty, took control of Jessore jail on Monday after scaring away guards with iron bars and knives.
The Jessore uprising led prisoners in Bangladesh's southern Barisal Jail to stage a short-lived mutiny out of solidarity on Thursday, police said.
Police said about 200 prisoners suddenly attacked guards with iron rods and bricks at noon, injuring 30 police at Barisal, 200 km (120 miles) south of Dhaka.
"The off-duty guards from nearby camps reinforced and overpowered the mutineers after an hour of fighting," said one police officer in Barisal.
He said about 100 prisoners were hurt in the incident.
The prisoners rioted out of solidarity with Jessore prisoners, police said. "We were just trying to express our solidarity," the police officer quoted prisoners as saying.

Meanwhile, the government tightened security around Jessore jail on Thursday as the prison revolt there entered its fourth day. Nearly 2,000 armed police and paramilitary troops have been put on alert around the complex, police said.
"We are ready for a raid but political leaders are still insisting on a peaceful end to the crisis," one police official at Jessore, 270 km (160 miles) west of Dhaka, told Reuters.
"We want no one here but the home minister," one police official quoted one of the prisoners as saying.
An aide to Home (interior) Minister Rafiqul Islam said the minister was not planning to go to Jessore.
Witnesses said authorities mobilised bulldozers, water cannon and ladders around the town centre jail compound ready to move when given the word.
Authorities on Wednesday called in extra troops from nearby districts and kept the public away.
Anxious relatives were trying to get near to the jail which holds about 3,000 prisoners, 300 of them women.
The trouble started after 90 prisoners were freed nationwide under an amnesty awarded as part of Monday's 25th independence anniversary celebrations.
Some were demanding freedom while others sought better food and treatment.
